newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Perry says U.S. to maintain security in Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Perry says U.S. to maintain security in Gulf.

text.p: U.S. Defense Secretary William Perry said on Friday the United States will keep eight radar-evading stealth fighters in Kuwait to deter aggression from Iran and Iraq.

"It is simply to maintain a strong deterrence in the region...as part of what we call a 'dual containment policy' in containing both Iraq and Iran and deal with any threat from either of these countries," Perry told a news conference in Kuwait during his visit to the Gulf region.
Perry held talks with Arab leaders in Kuwait and Qatar on Friday before flying to Saudi Arabia for meetings on Saturday and then on to the United Arab Emirates.
He will also visit the Prince Sultan Air Base in the Saudi desert, where some 4,000 U.S. troops have been moved to protect them from terrorist attack.
In Kuwait and Qatar, Perry visited areas where heavy American tanks and other weapons are being stored in case Iraq again invades Kuwait, as it did in 1990.
"Prepositioning is the key to deterrence of aggression in the Gulf region," Perry told a news conference in Qatar's capital Doha, before he flew on to Riyadh.
"It is indispensable for timely response to any crisis situation."
Perry was also asked about calls from some Gulf states for some degress of normalisation of relations with Iraq. "I think any such calls are premature," he said.
"The United States has no quarrel with the Iraqi people...but as long as he (Saddam Hussein) is the leader of the country, then I see no basis for normal, friendly relations."

Perry also said that the United States had been watching recent Iranian navel manoeuvres in the Gulf and noted that Iran had "been very careful" not to pose a threat to other countries or shipping with the manoeuvres.
"We watch carefully the Iranian Navy and we are not impressed," Perry told reporters in Doha.

Perry told the news conference that Gulf security was a "vital national security interest of the United States" and "the Clinton Administration was strongly committed to the security and the stability of the Gulf region.

Earlier in Kuwait Perry said the United States would remove 4,200 American troops from Kuwait by Christmas but would maintain 1,800 Marines aboard ships off-shore to be ready after U.S. troops leave Kuwait next month.

Three thousand of those U.S. army troops were sent to Kuwait in September along with the stealth fighters after Iraq troops intervened in northern Iraq to help one Kurdish faction in its fight with another Kurdish group.

When asked if Kuwait would allow the United States to use the stealth against Iran in a crisis, Kuwait Defence Minister Sheikh Salem Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah said their presence was to defend Kuwait against any aggression.

Perry had told a group of U.S. soldiers after talks with Kuwait's Crown Prince Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah and the defence minister that he had informed the Kuwaiti officials that the F-117A jets would stay as part of "a message to (Iraqi President) Saddam Hussein don't even think about coming back."
A U.S.-led military coalition defeated Saddam's forces in the 1991 Gulf War and drove Iraqi troops from Kuwait.

The stealth, other military hardware and ground U.S. troops, were rushed to Kuwait in September in a confrontation between the United States and Iraq over attacks by Iraq's military forces against Kurds in northern Iraq. They had been expected to return to the United States early next month.
During a visit on Friday to the aircraft carrier USS Kitty Hawk, Perry warned that Iraq and Iran had designs on controlling 70 percent of the world's oil reserves.
"Two countries" had designs on controlling "two thirds of world oil supplies located in the Gulf," Perry said. "I don't have to tell you who those two nations are -- they are Iraq and Iran."
Iran, the region's non-Arab power, controls the only entrance to the Gulf waterway, the narrow Strait of Hormuz through which 15 million barrels of oil pass every day, with Gulf Arab Oman.

Western powers and their Gulf Arab allies have in recent months repeatedly expressed concern over Iran's ambitious rearmament programme, saying it was a threat to the oil-rich region and far exceeds the Islamic republic's defensive needs.
The United States has 27 warships in and around the Gulf and some 200 warplanes.

Perry also said U.S. and Saudi Arabian intelligence efforts averted possible new "terrorist" attacks in the kingdom and the American military remains on high alert there. He said that there had been a number of arrests to prevent possible attacks in the kingdom.
A total of 24 U.S. soldiers were killed in two bomb attacks in Saudi Arabia in November, 1995, and in June of this year. Investigations continue into those incidents.

The Saudi government executed four Saudi citizens in the first bombing and Saudi authorities and the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation are cooperating in an inquiry into the June 25 blast at the military housing facility at Dhahran.
No culprits have been announced in the second bombing attack although published reports said the Saudis arrested as many as 40 people in connection with the investigation.
